$comment: FIXED PARALLEL WIDTHS THAT NO GRANT SIZES (agent/plans/PLAN-prepush-full-cpu.md PF9). The 2026-10-05 ruling removed every static worker count:
a parallel tool sizes itself from the cores granted at launch (core_lease.granted_cores(), grantedCores()). What stays fixed is request
concurrency against a remote API, which is not a core count (operator decision point, DEFAULT taken: I/O widths stay fixed and listed), and a
test fixture that needs an exact count. check:ci-record-paths refuses an unlisted literal width, a listed one that is gone or renumbered, and
every core cap such as min(8, os.cpu_count()), which cannot be listed. An entry is keyed on its file and its source text, never a line number.

widths.limit: none; the selftest parses the header of exactly two xdist workers
widths.reason: A header-parse fixture, not a width: the selftest asserts the `2 workers [N items]` line pytest-xdist prints, which needs exactly two workers whatever the host has (PF4 keeps it, and its comment says so).

widths.limit: GitHub REST API job-log downloads, under GitHub's secondary rate limits on concurrent requests
widths.reason: Concurrent job-log downloads from the GitHub REST API for the lane-budget variant sample (about 440 logs); the width bounds requests in flight against GitHub, not local cores.

widths.limit: GitHub REST API artifact downloads, under GitHub's secondary rate limits on concurrent requests
widths.reason: Concurrent unit-duration artifact zip downloads from the GitHub REST API (several hundred per ten-run sample); it matches VARIANT_LOG_WORKERS and bounds requests in flight, not cores.

widths.limit: Cloudflare R2 S3 API, server-side CopyObject requests
widths.reason: Parallel server-side CopyObject calls during the R2 release promote; the copies move no bytes through the runner, so the width bounds request concurrency against R2, not CPU or bandwidth.

widths.limit: Cloudflare R2 S3 API, server-side CopyObject requests
widths.reason: The promotion simulation's parallel CopyObject calls (PLAN-ci-time-budget T2.5 widened it from the twin's 8): small server-side R2 requests, so the width is request concurrency against R2.

widths.limit: Cloudflare R2 S3 API, server-side CopyObject requests
widths.reason: The bash twin of simulate_promotion.py: eight concurrent copy_one_object calls, each one aws s3api CopyObject request against R2, so the width bounds remote requests rather than local cores.

widths.limit: GitHub REST API via gh api, under GitHub's secondary rate limits on concurrent requests
widths.reason: Eight concurrent `gh api` calls (the `xargs -P 8` of audit.sh:125): every worker waits on a GitHub API response, so the width bounds requests in flight against GitHub, not local cores.

widths.limit: the media CDN serving tutorial words.json files, about 180 fetches per run
widths.reason: Concurrent remote fetches of tutorial words.json files (about 180 per run, each retried on 5xx); the workers wait on the CDN, so the width bounds requests in flight, not local cores.

widths.limit: third-party web hosts named by external links, kept polite to avoid 429s
widths.reason: Concurrent HTTP probes of external links on third-party hosts with a 15 s timeout; the width keeps the gate polite to hosts that rate-limit, and no worker does CPU work of its own.
